title: A simple, rapid and very efficient protocol for DNA isolation from mosquito species
protocol: Wash preserved mosquitoes in sterile distilled water or PBS to remove excess alcohol.
Grind mosquitoes directly if fresh, using a micropipette tip in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube with 50-100 µl of 1X STE buffer and 100 mM sucrose.
Add 1X STE buffer to reach a total volume of 300-500 µl for single mosquitoes or 1 ml for mosquito pools.
Add 1% SDS, 1% Triton-X, 10 µl/ml Rnase A (20 mg/ml), and 20 µl/ml Proteinase K (20 mg/ml).
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour and 30 minutes, gently mixing every 15 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Add equal volume of phenol:chloroform (1:1), shake well for 5 minutes, and centrifuge at 12,000g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Repeat the previous step with chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) and centrifuge under the same conditions.
Transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh tube, add two-fold volume of cold isopropanol, and incubate at -20°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge at 12,000g for 30 minutes at 4°C, then remove the supernatant.
Incubate the dry pellet at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Dissolve the dry pellet in nuclease-free water or TE buffer (pH 8.0).
